newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson wins Sri Lanka contract.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson wins Sri Lanka contract.

text.p: Swedish telecom group LM Ericsson AB said on Monday it had won a contract worth 335 million crowns ($50.5 million) for supply and installation of a radio access telecommunications network in Sri Lanka.

"Ericsson has signed a turnkey contract worth 335 million crowns with Telia Lanka for the supply of a complete telecommunications to be installed in Greater Colombo and the Kandy area as well as the areas north and south of the capital," Ericsson said in a statement.

The contract involves Ericsson delivering and installing the network that includes its radio access system DRA 1900, based on Digital Enhanced Cordless Tgelecommunications (DECT) standard, and AXE switching equipment.
Ericsson will also deliver a complete management system.
Telia Lanka is an operator joint-venture between the Sri Lankan parties Metropolitan and the National Development Bank and the Swedish operator Telia.
This year Telia Lanka was granted a licence to provide basic telephone services in Sri Lanka by means of radio access.
